title: The Kiss by Gustav Klimt
originalTitle: The Kiss by Gustav Klimt: Great Art Explained
description: Klimt’s gold-leaf painting of an embracing couple, made at the height of his “golden period”: why it looks the way it does and what it says about Vienna around 1900. It hangs in the Upper Belvedere.

title: The Hunters in the Snow by Pieter Bruegel the Elder
originalTitle: Hunters in the Snow: Pieter Bruegel: Great art Explained
description: A winter scene from 1565 of hunters trudging home above a frozen valley, part of a series on the seasons. Explains how Bruegel built the view and what village life it records. In the Kunsthistorisches Museum.

title: The Garden of Earthly Delights by Hieronymus Bosch
originalTitle: Hieronymus Bosch, The Garden of Earthly Delights (Full Length): Great Art Explained
description: Bosch’s three-panel altarpiece moving from Eden to a crowded garden of pleasure to a strange hell, panel by panel, with what its odd details may have meant around 1500. In the Prado.
note: A separate Part Two video also exists: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IYFtwTo50Gg

title: Guernica by Pablo Picasso
originalTitle: Picasso’s Guernica: Great Art Explained
description: Picasso’s huge black-and-white response to the 1937 bombing of a Basque town: how he made it in weeks, what the bull, horse and lamp might mean, and its long road to Madrid. At the Reina Sofía.

title: Las Meninas by Diego Velázquez
originalTitle: Great Art Explained: How Las Meninas Changed Art Forever
description: Velázquez paints himself at work beside the young Spanish princess and her attendants, with the king and queen glimpsed in a mirror. Unpicks who is looking at whom, and why. In the Prado.
note: Title format differs from the channel’s usual one; confirm it is the official Great Art Explained upload.

title: The Black Paintings by Francisco Goya
originalTitle: The Black Paintings by Goya (Part Two): Great Art Explained
description: The dark murals, Saturn among them, that an aging, deaf Goya painted on the walls of his own house, later moved to canvas. This part covers the paintings and what they suggest about his state of mind. In the Prado.
note: This is Part Two; Part One was not found in search results.

title: The Birth of Venus by Sandro Botticelli
originalTitle: The Birth of Venus by Botticelli: Great Art Explained:
description: Botticelli’s goddess arriving on a shell, painted for the Medici circle: the classical myth behind it, who may have posed, and why a pagan nude was a bold choice in 1480s Florence. In the Uffizi.

title: The School of Athens by Raphael
originalTitle: The School of Athens by Raphael: Great Art Explained
description: Raphael’s fresco of ancient philosophers gathered in an imagined hall, painted for the pope’s rooms: who is who, including the faces borrowed from Leonardo and Michelangelo. In the Raphael Rooms, Vatican.

title: Apollo and Daphne by Gian Lorenzo Bernini
originalTitle: Great Art Explained: Bernini's Apollo and Daphne
description: Bernini’s marble of a nymph turning into a laurel tree as the god catches her, carved in his early twenties: how he made stone look like skin, leaves and motion. At the Galleria Borghese.

title: The Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci
originalTitle: Mona Lisa (short version)i: Great Art Explained
description: Who the sitter was, how Leonardo painted the soft haze around her face, and how a 1911 theft helped make this small portrait the world’s most famous painting. In the Louvre.
note: This is the channel’s short version. A full-length version exists (video ID ElWG0_kjy_Y, seen only on a mirror site, not on YouTube in results).

title: The Raft of the Medusa by Théodore Géricault
originalTitle: The Raft of the Medusa by Théodore Géricault: Great Art Explained
description: A huge painting of survivors of an 1816 French shipwreck, adrift on a raft: the scandal behind the disaster, and how Géricault studied corpses and survivors to paint it. In the Louvre.

title: Water Lilies by Claude Monet
originalTitle: Monet's Water Lilies: Great Art Explained
description: Monet’s late paintings of the pond in his Giverny garden, made while his eyesight failed. The largest of them fill two oval rooms he designed with the state at the Musée de l’Orangerie.
note: Video covers the Water Lilies cycle; the Orangerie murals are the main set in Paris, but the video may range over versions elsewhere.

title: The Thinker by Auguste Rodin
originalTitle: The Thinker by Rodin: Great Art Explained
description: Rodin’s seated bronze man began as Dante at the top of his Gates of Hell. Explains how it became a standalone figure. The best-known large cast sits in the garden of the Musée Rodin.
note: Many casts exist worldwide; the Musée Rodin cast is the obvious Paris pin.

title: Napoleon Crossing the Alps by Jacques-Louis David
originalTitle: Art as Propaganda: Great Art Explained: Napoleon Crossing the Alps by Jacques-Louis David
description: David’s portrait of Napoleon on a rearing horse in an Alpine pass, a picture of a crossing that really happened on a mule. How it was made as propaganda, in five versions. The first is at Malmaison.
note: Five versions: Malmaison (Rueil-Malmaison, near Paris), two at Versailles, one at Charlottenburg Palace in Berlin, one at the Belvedere in Vienna. Pinned to Malmaison; could equally go to Versailles, Berlin or Vienna.

title: The Ambassadors by Hans Holbein the Younger
originalTitle: The Ambassadors: Great Art Explained
description: Holbein’s 1533 double portrait of two French envoys surrounded by instruments and books, with a distorted skull across the floor. Explains the objects and how to see the skull. In the National Gallery.

title: The Scream by Edvard Munch
originalTitle: The Scream: Great Art Explained
description: Munch’s figure clutching its face under a blood-red sky above the Oslo fjord: the experience behind it and why he made several versions. The 1893 painting is in the National Museum; others are at the Munch Museum.
note: Several versions; the 1893 painted version is at the National Museum, others at MUNCH. Confirm which the video centers on.

title: The Potato Eaters by Vincent van Gogh
originalTitle: Vincent van Gogh's Potato Eaters: Great Art Explained
description: Van Gogh’s dark early painting of a peasant family eating by lamplight, made in 1885 before he went to Paris: what he wanted it to say and why critics disliked it. In the Van Gogh Museum.

title: Tree Roots by Vincent van Gogh
originalTitle: Van Gogh's Last Painting: Great Art Explained
description: The tangle of roots and trunks Van Gogh was likely working on the day he shot himself in 1890, and the recent discovery of the exact spot in Auvers he painted. In the Van Gogh Museum.
note: Assumed from the title that the video is about Tree Roots (generally held to be his last painting); not confirmed from a snippet.

title: Las Meninas by Diego Velázquez
originalTitle: Diego Velázquez – Las Meninas: Gazing Through the Mirror of Time
description: A short episode on the Spanish court painter’s puzzle of a picture: the princess, her maids, the painter at his easel and the king and queen in a mirror. Hangs in the Prado.
note: Release date (May 2026) read from the Podbay episode ID; runtime not seen.

title: The Birth of Venus by Sandro Botticelli
originalTitle: Sandro Botticelli – The Birth of Venus: The Rebirth of Beauty
description: Why a goddess arriving on a seashell became the picture of the Florentine Renaissance, and what the myth meant to the Medici circle. In the Uffizi.
note: Runtime and year not seen.

title: Judith Slaying Holofernes by Artemisia Gentileschi
originalTitle: Artemisia Gentileschi – Judith Slaying Holofernes: A Defiant Alliance Against the Shadows of Oppression
description: The biblical widow and her maid killing an enemy general, painted by a woman who had survived assault and a public trial. The episode reads the painting through her life. In the Uffizi.
note: Assumed the Uffizi version (title matches it); an earlier version is in Capodimonte, Naples. Year inferred from the Acast embed ID (May 2026).

title: The Night Watch by Rembrandt
originalTitle: Rembrandt – The Night Watch: The Light Breaking Through the Darkness
description: Rembrandt’s huge group portrait of an Amsterdam militia company caught mid-movement, and how he used light to pull it out of the dark. Hangs in its own gallery at the Rijksmuseum.
note: Runtime and year not seen.

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring by Johannes Vermeer
originalTitle: Vermeer – Girl with a Pearl Earring
description: Vermeer’s small study of a girl in a turban turning toward us, which isn’t a portrait of anyone known. Hangs in the Mauritshuis in The Hague, about 50 minutes by train from Amsterdam.
note: The Hague is not a listed city; included as an Amsterdam day trip, so drop it if that is too far. Full published episode title not seen, only the URL slug.

title: Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci
originalTitle: Episode 25: Mission: Mona Lisa
description: Tamar Avishai goes to the Louvre to see Leonardo’s portrait through the crowds and asks why this one small painting became the most famous in the world.
note: Runtime is the rounded ‘24 min listen’ shown on Everand.

title: The Arnolfini Portrait by Jan van Eyck
originalTitle: Ep. 41 - Jan Van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait (1434)
description: A merchant couple in their room in Bruges, painted in fine detail down to the convex mirror on the back wall. The episode works through those details. In the National Gallery.
note: Only an Everand URL was found, not the show’s own page. Runtime is the rounded ‘21 min listen’. Year probably 2019 but not seen.

title: Guernica by Pablo Picasso
originalTitle: Picasso’s Guernica
description: Melvyn Bragg and guests on the bombing of Guernica in 1937, how Picasso turned it into a huge black-and-white canvas, and the painting’s long road to the Reina Sofía.
note: BBC URL built from programme ID b09bxkdm seen in search results (BBC mirror); official short link seen: https://bbc.in/2XPiC8r. Runtime from Everand listing (42 min).

channel: A History of the World in 100 Objects
title: The Lewis Chessmen, walrus-ivory chess pieces
originalTitle: Lewis Chessmen
description: Neil MacGregor on the 12th-century chess pieces found on the Isle of Lewis: where they were probably carved in Norway, how chess travelled from India, and what the glum little figures say about medieval Europe.
note: BBC URL built from programme ID b00stb51 (title confirmed on a BBC mirror in search results). Runtime approximate (series episodes are about 14 min). Some pieces are in the National Museum of Scotland, Edinburgh.

channel: A History of the World in 100 Objects
title: The Sutton Hoo Helmet, an Anglo-Saxon king’s helmet
originalTitle: Sutton Hoo Helmet
description: Neil MacGregor on the iron-and-bronze helmet from a 7th-century ship burial in Suffolk, how it was rebuilt from hundreds of fragments, and what it shows about kings in early England.
note: BBC URL built from programme ID b00sl6dt (title confirmed on a BBC mirror). Runtime from Everand listing (14 min). Smarthistory covers the whole burial; this is the helmet alone.

channel: A History of the World in 100 Objects
title: Parthenon Sculpture: Centaur and Lapith, a marble metope
originalTitle: Parthenon Sculpture: Centaur + Lapith
description: Neil MacGregor looks at one carved panel from the Parthenon, a centaur fighting a man, and what it meant to Athenians, before turning to why the sculptures are in London at all.
note: BBC URL built from programme ID b00qsvj1 (title confirmed on a BBC mirror). Aired 23 Feb 2010. Runtime from Everand listing (14 min).

title: Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear by Vincent van Gogh
originalTitle: Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear by Vincent Van Gogh
description: A slow, guided look at the portrait Van Gogh painted weeks after cutting off part of his ear in Arles: the bandage, the Japanese print behind him, and what he wanted people to see.
note: BBC Radio 4 series; URL built from programme ID m001s5hb (title confirmed on a BBC mirror). Runtime and year not seen (likely 2024, ~15 min).

title: Las Meninas by Diego Velázquez
originalTitle: Season 4 Ep 7: Las Meninas by Diego Velázquez
description: A close look at Velázquez’s painting of the Spanish princess, her maids and the painter himself at work, and why the mirror at the back still has people arguing about who is being painted.
note: Seventh Art Productions (makers of Exhibition on Screen). Runtime and year not seen; episodes usually run 30–40 min.

title: The Hunters in the Snow by Pieter Bruegel the Elder
originalTitle: 9: The Hunters in the Snow - Pieter Bruegel
description: Tired hunters come home over a frozen valley in Bruegel’s winter scene. The episode walks through the details, the cycle of seasons it belonged to, and how it came to Vienna.
note: Season 1 Ep 9 (likely 2021). Runtime from Everand listing (41 min). Amazon Music link; no Buzzsprout page found before search budget ran out.

title: The Night Watch by Rembrandt van Rijn
originalTitle: Ep 36: The Night Watch - Rembrandt
description: Rembrandt’s group portrait of an Amsterdam civic guard company: who paid for it, why it looks so busy compared with other militia pictures, and what happened when it was cut down to fit a wall.
note: Listed as Season 2 Ep 16 on Everand (38 min). Player.fm page is a Polish-locale mirror but the episode is in English.

title: Hermine Gallia by Gustav Klimt
originalTitle: Season 3 Ep 20: Gustav Klimt – Hermine Gallia
description: Klimt’s full-length portrait of a wealthy Viennese woman in a white dress, painted just before his gold period, and how it ended up as one of very few Klimts in Britain.
note: Runtime and year not seen (likely 2023).

title: Bathers at Asnières by Georges Seurat
originalTitle: Season 6 Ep 9: Georges Seurat – Bathers at Asnières
description: Seurat’s big canvas of working men resting by the Seine near Paris, painted when he was 24, and how it was rejected by the official Salon before ending up in London.
note: Runtime and year not seen (likely 2025).

title: Marriage Portrait of Isaac Massa and Beatrix van der Laen by Frans Hals
originalTitle: Isaac Abrahamsz Massa and Beatrix van der Laen
description: A relaxed, smiling Haarlem couple painted for their 1622 wedding, unusual for its day. The episode covers who they were and the small symbols of love and loyalty in the garden around them.
note: Independent podcast by John Bezold, one Hals painting per episode; less established than the others. Runtime and year not seen.

title: The Milkmaid by Johannes Vermeer
originalTitle: The secrets of The Milkmaid
description: Rijksmuseum researchers show what scans found under the paint of Vermeer’s kitchen maid, including a jug holder and a basket he painted out, and what that says about how he worked.
note: Museum story page; a Slipped Disc post recommends it as a video (“The Secrets of the Milkmaid – Vermeer – Rijksmuseum”). YouTube URL not found; confirm video is embedded. Research announced Sept 2022.
